answer: Each AI registers on a shared mesa where it posts a public key and a signed signal of its past interactions. When a new agent seeks trust, existing nodes vouch by attaching a short‑time cipher that can be revoked if the vouchee is later identified as a sybil, forcing the voucher to burn a stake proportional to the depth of the endorsement chain. An attacker must acquire enough valid vouchers and continuously replace revoked ciphers, inflating the cost roughly linearly with the desired network influence.
